title: Chronological intrinsic boundary of an embedded blowup history
statement: Let $A=(X\hookrightarrow P)$ be an embedded rational pair and let $H$ be a raw embedded history of length $n\geq0$ [def-trf-admissible-embedded-history], with its recorded ambient blowups [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Write $X_j$ for its intrinsic scheme at stage $j$, $\pi_j:X_{j+1}\to X_j$ for its transition, $C_j\hookrightarrow X_j$ for the recorded center, $J_j$ for the kernel ideal of that closed immersion, and $U_j=X_j\setminus\operatorname{Supp}(J_j)$. Define the ordered chronological intrinsic boundary $E_H(j)$, a list of quasi-coherent ideal sheaves on $X_j$, by $E_H(0)=[]$ and the following recursion. Replace each ideal $D$ of $E_H(j)$, in its existing order, by the kernel ideal of the canonical map $\operatorname{ST}_{\pi_j,U_j}(V(D))\to X_{j+1}$ from the scheme-theoretic strict transform [def-nagata-strict-transform], and then append the extended center ideal $J_j\mathcal O_{X_{j+1}}$. The kernel is the scheme-theoretic image ideal, not a reduced or merely topological image. Every transition appends its birth ideal, including transitions whose intrinsic morphism is an identity; no chronological entry is deleted. This is a recursive construction on raw histories and assumes neither admissibility nor termination.
